object_description: five-story elongated building with recessed upper level and arcade
design_condition: Placed on the southern edge, the elongated volume connects to the existing base, defines a street-level central square, and reshapes the adjoining outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The elongated volume is embedded convincingly in the topographically difficult situation and defines an attractive central square.

position.rationale: The elongated mass visibly frames a street-level open area along its southern edge.

positive.statement: The orthogonal development pattern fits the existing buildings and supports legibility.

position.rationale: Regular orthogonal edges and repeated levels are clear across the plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The public-intensive uses are coherently oriented toward the square and can be combined effectively.

position.rationale: A plausible lower southern zone faces the visible central square.

positive.statement: The arcade living typology corresponds positively to campus living, and the floor-by-floor division of housing types is convincing.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal bands and recessed edges indicate an arcade-like residential zone.

positive.statement: The recessed upper level is volumetrically clever and provides a covered outdoor area with functional advantages.

position.rationale: The upper mass is visibly set back, leaving a covered edge below.

positive.statement: The proposed timber construction is structurally well thought through, while the rooms have a pleasant simplicity and directness.

position.rationale: The sampled building envelope supports a broad structural and spatial reading, though rooms are not resolved.

positive.statement: The planted arcade promises a high quality of stay through climate-regulating vegetation.

position.rationale: The southern edge provides the most plausible location for the planted arcade.

negative.statement: The position of the multi-purpose hall behind the new stairs is somewhat unfavorable.

position.rationale: A lower southern access zone is plausible, but the hall and stairs are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The studios and apartments are generally sparsely lit, and the direct entry into the living-dining area is critically questioned.

position.rationale: Residential rooms are approximated along the southern envelope; interior lighting and entry conditions are unresolved.

negative.statement: The rational grid cannot be maintained across the different housing offerings, the wet cells are poorly stacked, and the top-floor static system is unconvincing.

position.rationale: Upper residential structure is broadly anchored to the visible mass, without interior system evidence.

negative.statement: The external-space visualization and proposed materiality read as two unrelated worlds, so the intention cannot be clearly understood.

position.rationale: The southern building-edge and adjoining open-space interface is the relevant visible comparison zone.

negative.statement: The flat open-space concept seals large areas and sacrifices some mature trees without the visualized species-rich planting being evident.

position.target: flat open-space concept and mature trees
position.rationale: A peripheral southern site area is indicated, but paving and tree species are not represented distinctly.

negative.statement: Planting the wooden structure with climbing plants may create problems for longevity.

position.rationale: The likely planted facade aligns with the southern arcade, though climbing vegetation is not visible.

negative.statement: The green roof appears to have only a thin substrate layer, with no apparent use of the roof areas.

position.rationale: The roof plane is visible at the recessed upper footprint; substrate depth and use remain indeterminate.
